clue.text: Light on bed close to wall has switches

indicators.note: to switch things is to swap them about, so these letters change places
the close of a word is its final letter, so take the end of wall

explanation.surface: A lamp sits on the bed by the wall, with its switches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' takes L, the last letter of 'wall'; 'switches' then rearranges ON BED, L and HAS into ASH BLONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash blonde is a very pale hair colour, so it describes light hair.

clue.text: In a film about democracy, only the leader survives

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the haze goes round the letter

parts.note: a film is a thin haze or coating, like a mist

indicators.note: only the leading letter of democracy is kept

explanation.surface: A political film about democracy in which only the leader is left alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are prepositions of position: to be amid things is to be in among them.

clue.text: Row out of port with sailor, having a short recce

parts.note: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire
AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a recce (reconnaissance) is a look round

explanation.surface: Rowing out of harbour with a seaman, taking a quick look about.
explanation.definitionFit: A row in the sense of a noisy disturbance is a hullabaloo, an uproar.

clue.text: Deal finally taking off, not a time for cutting back

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word deal
not says these letters are left out of the word that precedes them

parts.note: taking someone off is mimicking or imitating them
A is taken as written and T is the usual abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A deal is finally coming off, at a bad time for spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' looks like departing; it means mimicking. 'not' drops A and T from the mimicry word.
explanation.definitionFit: Limiting spending or output is restricting it, a form of cutting back.

clue.text: What's snack shop unwrapped separately?

indicators.note: each word loses its outer letters on its own, as if each wrapping were removed

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what one gets from a snack shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip each word of its first and last letters: snack gives NAC and shop gives HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla-chip snack, and the clue as a whole describes one.

clue.text: Words to assassin from short fat revolutionary—— peculiarly true

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the shortened word is read backwards
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: butter is a cooking fat

indicators.note: peculiarly means oddly, so the letters of true are rearranged

explanation.surface: Words for an assassin from a short, fat revolutionary, oddly true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts BUTTER to BUTTE, which 'revolutionary' turns into ETTUB; 'peculiarly' makes RUTE from TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's reproach to Brutus, one of his killers, in Shakespeare's play is these famous words.

clue.text: Slave ship replacing destroyer's centre stage

indicators.note: replacing says one set of letters takes another's place
the centre stage of the word is its middle part, the bit that is swapped out

parts.note: a vandal is a wrecker or destroyer
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A slave ship takes the place of a destroyer in the middle of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' and 'centre stage' put SS in place of ND, the middle of VANDAL. The blog first thought 'stage' was superfluous; read it as 'part'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal was a feudal subordinate, and loosely a servile dependant or slave.

clue.text: Drive off, missing end of film

indicators.note: missing end of says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to film a scene is to shoot it

explanation.surface: Driving away before the end of the film.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoo animals or people is to wave them away, driving them off.

clue.text: Break twisted felt that's got wound around

indicators.note: around says the wound word goes round the twisted letters

parts.note: to wound is to harm

indicators.note: twisted means the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A broken piece of twisted felt, with something wound around it.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-term is a short holiday in the middle of a British school term; 'twisted' scrambles the felt and 'around' wraps the wound round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A school half-term holiday is a short break from lessons.

clue.text: Drawing back, clutching long pipe

indicators.note: clutching means holding inside, so one piece is held within the other
back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: drawing is a branch of art
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Someone inhaling, holding on to a long pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' is not inhaling but art; 'back' turns it round and 'clutching' has it hold the longing.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe carrying air to the lungs.

clue.text: Religion's making mark in lives of ordinary people

parts.note: lives means is, as in to be or exist

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: laic means of the laity, ordinary people rather than clergy
M is short for the German mark

explanation.surface: A religion making its mark on the lives of ordinary folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamic means belonging to the faith of Islam, so it is a religion's adjective.

clue.text: Cod sent back following admission of error

indicators.note: sent back means the word is turned round

parts.note: oops is what you say on making a mistake
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A fishmonger sending back the cod after admitting a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns OOPS into SPOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod as an adjective means mock or parody, and a spoof is just that.

clue.text: Be stingy with a fortune? You might let me off!

parts.note: read as sting-y, to be like a sting is to smart
costing a bomb means costing a fortune in British slang

explanation.surface: A miser pleading to be let off after hoarding a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be stingy' is a pun: not mean, but stinging, which is to smart. 'You might let me off!' is a cryptic definition, a bomb being let off.
explanation.definitionFit: A guided bomb is something one lets off, so the exclamation is a playful cryptic description of it.

clue.text: Fall back on drinks and drug

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
a cat laps, that is drinks, milk
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Falling back on drink and drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to slip back into an old illness or habit.

clue.text: Officer and girl go below to fix a drink

indicators.note: in a down entry the officer and girl come below the earlier pieces

parts.note: to pin something is to fix it in place
COL is the abbreviation for colonel
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An officer and a girl go downstairs to mix a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A pina colada is a rum, pineapple and coconut cocktail, a mixed drink.

clue.text: Statesman once out of favour henceforth backed

indicators.note: backed says the hidden letters are read backwards
out of says the letters are taken from within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A former statesman out of favour from now on.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'out' in the definition, leaving the hidden word with no indicator; 'out of' signals the run, and 'backed' turns URHEN round.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, a statesman of the past.

clue.text: Colorado construction engineers move road south of hospital

indicators.note: in a down entry the rearranged letters sit beneath the first piece

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

indicators.note: engineers as a verb means contrives or rearranges

explanation.surface: Engineers diverting a road to the south of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineers' rearranges MOVE ROAD into OOVERDAM, placed after H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hoover Dam is a huge dam built across the Colorado River.

clue.text: Crack guards useful in the extreme for prison camps

indicators.note: guards means holds within, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a crack is a joke, a gag

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Crack guards proving useful in running prison camps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the extreme' gives U and L, the ends of 'useful', which go inside GAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulag was the Soviet system of forced labour camps.

clue.text: Succeed, having good work accessories to boot

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
laces are fittings for a boot

explanation.surface: Succeeding, with good work accessories thrown in as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to boot' looks like 'as well'; it means for a boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who will go places is set to succeed in life.

clue.text: What makes ham have fatal ingredient?

indicators.note: what makes asks for the change that turns one word into the next

parts.note: turning the first word into the second needs VE added and no M

explanation.surface: Asking what ingredient makes ham deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as VE, NO M: add VE and lose the M, and ham becomes have.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is poison, the deadly substance in a snake's bite.

clue.text: Great player spinning round's eliminated half of rivals

indicators.note: spinning means the whole run is turned round

parts.note: a round is an O, and the 's is S
a player eliminated is out

indicators.note: half of takes the first three letters of rivals

explanation.surface: A great player's rivals are knocked out of the round by spin.
explanation.walkthrough: OSOUTRIV, read backwards under 'spinning', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a performer of outstanding skill, especially in music.

clue.text: Fail to justify cut with old daggers

indicators.note: cut means the end is chopped off

parts.note: to belie something is to show it false, failing to justify it

explanation.surface: Failing to justify a stabbing with old daggers.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are printers' dagger marks, used for footnotes or doubtful passages.

clue.text: Truncated storyline accompanies very short film about Bulgarian city

indicators.note: truncated means cut short, losing its end

parts.note: a storyline is a plot
V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round

parts.note: vid is short for video, a film

explanation.surface: A cut-down storyline goes with a short film about a city in Bulgaria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very short' is the standard abbreviation V; 'about' turns the short word for a video round.
explanation.definitionFit: Plovdiv is Bulgaria's second city.

clue.text: Provide transport for doctor removing one's elderly patient?

parts.note: to do food or drinks is to provide them

indicators.note: removing says the following letters are taken out

parts.note: the TARDIS is the time machine of Doctor Who, the BBC science fiction hero
one is I, and 's gives S

explanation.surface: Arranging transport for a doctor who is taking an old patient away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' here is Doctor Who, of the long-running BBC series, whose TARDIS is a time-travelling police box.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotard is a senile old person, the kind of elderly patient a doctor might see.

clue.text: Tenant not so keen to give up housing

parts.note: less means not so much

indicators.note: the outer letters are the housing round the middle, and they are dropped

explanation.surface: A tenant who is less eager to give up the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee is someone who holds property on a lease, a tenant.

clue.text: Conductor returned to office, then travelled on

parts.note: a candidate returned to office is voted in, as in president elect
to ride is to travel on a horse or bike, so rode is past

explanation.surface: A conductor re-elected to office, then travelling on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests a musician or bus worker; it is the electrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves.

clue.text: Rules of race banning indefinite number

indicators.note: banning means excluding, so a letter is removed

parts.note: ethnic means relating to race
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Racial rules banning an unspecified number.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles, rules of conduct.

clue.text: Scotsman's missing air among the most celebrated?

indicators.note: missing says the following word is dropped

parts.note: Alistair is a typically Scottish first name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman without airs, wondering if he is among the famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the top tier of celebrities, the most famous people.

clue.text: The sides to cheer out, fit for a crunch game.

indicators.note: out says these letters are removed

parts.note: something crispy is good for crunching

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fans told to cheer on the sides, fit for a crunch match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sides to cheer' gives C and R, which 'out' removes from CRISPY. I-spy is a children's guessing game.
explanation.definitionFit: I-spy is a children's guessing game played by naming things one can see.

clue.text: House connected to well has complex pipes

parts.note: OK means well or fine

indicators.note: complex means intricate, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A house connected to a well has complicated plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' makes OKAHS from OK and HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hookahs are oriental tobacco pipes that draw smoke through water.

clue.text: Stores more IPA for a bash

indicators.note: a bash is a blow, knocking the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Laying in more India Pale Ale for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' (a party, but here a knock) rearranges MORE IPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia, the plural of emporium, are large shops or stores.

clue.text: Note bird with stuffing in saved for oven

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
a crow is a bird

indicators.note: the stuffing of a word is its inside, everything but the ends

explanation.surface: A recipe note: the bird with its stuffing kept for the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffing in' gives AVE, the middle of 'saved'.
explanation.definitionFit: A microwave is a kitchen oven that cooks with radiation.
